## Why This Is Asked

- Cloud Deploy multi-region rollout
- Traffic Director regional routing
- Artifact Registry build/push workflow
- Cloud Monitoring alerts and SLO/SLI linkage

```yaml
# clouddeploy.yaml
apiVersion: deploy.cloud.google.com/v1
kind: Rollout
metadata:
  name: order-service-v4-rollout
spec:
  targets:
  - name: us-east1
  - name: us-central1
  - name: us-west1
  strategy:
    progressiveDelivery:
      trafficSplit:
        order-service-v4: 10
        order-service-v3: 90
```

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question validates expertise in multi-project Google Cloud architectures, progressive delivery patterns, and operational reliability using native tools.

## Key Concepts
- **Workload Identity Federation**: Secure cross-project service authentication without service account keys
- **Cloud Run per-revision traffic splits**: Granular traffic routing at the revision level
- **Cloud CDN integration**: Caching at the edge with load balancer
- **Cloud Monitoring with MQL**: Custom alerting based on latency and error thresholds
- **Cloud Run Invoker role**: Minimal IAM for service-to-service authentication

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Build and Push v2 to Artifact Registry (Project B)
```bash
# Enable required APIs
gcloud services enable run.googleapis.com artifactregistry.googleapis.com --project=PROJECT-B

# Create Artifact Registry repository
gcloud artifact repositories create cloud-run-source --repository-format=docker --location=us-central1 --project=PROJECT-B

# Build and push v2
docker build -t us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/project-b/cloud-run-source/v2:latest .
docker push us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/project-b/cloud-run-source/v2:latest
```

### 2. Deploy v2 to Cloud Run (Project B)
```bash
gcloud run deploy service-v2 \
  --image us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/project-b/cloud-run-source/v2:latest \
  --platform managed \
  --region us-central1 \
  --project PROJECT-B
```

### 3. Configure Cross-Project IAM with Workload Identity (Project A → B)
```bash
# In Project B, create workload identity pool
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools create cross-project-pool \
  --location=global \
  --project=PROJECT-B

# Allow Project A service account to impersonate
gcloud iam workload-identity-pools add-iam-policy-binding cross-project-pool \
  --location=global \
  --member="serviceAccount:PROJECT-A.svc.id.goog[default/cross-runner-sa]" \
  --role="roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser" \
  --project=PROJECT-B

# Grant Cloud Run Invoker to Project A's identity
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding service-v2 \
  --member=principal://iam.googleapis.com/projects/PROJECT-B/locations/global/workloadIdentityPools/cross-project-pool/subject/cross-runner \
  --role=roles/run.invoker \
  --project=PROJECT-B
```

### 4. Configure Load Balancer Traffic Split (Project A)
```bash
# Get v2 revision name
V2_REVISION=$(gcloud run revisions list --service=service-v2 --platform=managed --region=us-central1 --project=PROJECT-B --format='value(metadata.name)' | head -1)

# Set initial 5% traffic to v2
gcloud run services update-traffic service-v1 \
  --to-revisions=$V2_REVISION=5 \
  --platform managed \
  --region us-central1 \
  --project PROJECT-A

# For additional regions, repeat with respective regional endpoints
```

### 5. Create Cloud Monitoring Alert Policies (Project A)
```bash
# Alert for p95 latency > 450ms
gcloud alpha monitoring policies create \
  --notification-channels=EMAIL_CHANNEL \
  --display-name="v2 p95 Latency Alert" \
  --condition-display-name="p95 Latency > 450ms" \
  --condition-filter="resource.type=\"cloud_run_revision\" AND resource.labels.service=\"service-v2\" AND metric.type=\"run.googleapis.com/container_latency\"" \
  --condition-threshold-value=450 \
  --condition-threshold-duration=300s \
  --condition-threshold-comparison=COMPARISON_GT \
  --condition-aggregations="alignmentPeriod=300s,perSeriesAligner=ALIGN_PERCENTILE_95" \
  --project=PROJECT-A

# Alert for error rate > 1%
gcloud alpha monitoring policies create \
  --notification-channels=EMAIL_CHANNEL \
  --display-name="v2 Error Rate Alert" \
  --condition-filter="resource.type=\"cloud_run_revision\" AND resource.labels.service=\"service-v2\" AND metric.type=\"run.googleapis.com/container_request_count\" AND metric.labels.response_code_class>=\"500\"" \
  --condition-threshold-value=0.01 \
  --condition-threshold-duration=300s \
  --condition-threshold-comparison=COMPARISON_GT \
  --condition-aggregations="alignmentPeriod=300s,perSeriesAligner=ALIGN_RATE" \
  --project=PROJECT-A
```

### 6. Rollback by Traffic Shift
```bash
# Rollback: shift 100% traffic back to v1
gcloud run services update-traffic service-v1 \
  --to-revisions=v1-revision=100 \
  --platform managed \
  --region us-central1 \
  --project PROJECT-A
```

## Minimal IAM Roles Required
| Principal | Role | Purpose |
|-----------|------|---------|
| Pipeline Service Account (Project A) | `roles/run.invoker` on v2 (Project B) | Invoke v2 service |
| Pipeline Service Account (Project A) | `roles/run.admin` on services (Project A) | Manage traffic splits |
| Workload Identity User | `roles/iam.workloadIdentityUser` (Project B) | Impersonate Project B service account |
| Monitoring Alert Service Account | `roles/monitoring.alertPolicyEditor` (Project A) | Create and manage alerts |

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests practical blue/green deployment workflows, traffic splitting, and automated rollback capabilities using native GCP tools. It connects deployment mechanics with monitoring and access control—critical skills for operating reliable cloud-native applications.

## Key Concepts
- **Blue/Green Deployments**: Running two separate Cloud Run services (v1 and v2) behind a load balancer enables zero-downtime releases and easy rollback
- **Global HTTP(S) Load Balancer**: URL maps and backend services route traffic between service versions with configurable weights
- **Artifact Registry**: Stores container images built via Cloud Build or local docker builds
- **Cloud Monitoring**: Provides metrics for latency and error rate; alerts can trigger automated remediation
- **Cloud Functions/Workflows**: Execute rollback logic when thresholds are breached
- **IAM**: Minimal roles for build service, deployment automation, and monitoring

## Step-by-Step Implementation

1. **Build and push v2 to Artifact Registry**
```bash
gcloud builds submit --tag us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/image-processor/image-processor-v2 .
```

2. **Deploy v2 as separate Cloud Run service**
```bash
gcloud run deploy image-processor-v2 \
  --image us-central1-docker.pkg.dev/$PROJECT_ID/image-processor/image-processor-v2 \
  --region us-central1 \
  --platform managed
```

3. **Configure Load Balancer traffic splitting**
```bash
gcloud compute backend-services update image-processor-backend \
  --load-balancing-scheme=EXTERNAL \
  --custom-request-header="X-Canary: true"
```
Create a URL map with matching rules to route 20% of requests to the v2 backend service.

4. **Set up monitoring alerts**
- Create a Cloud Monitoring alert policy for p95 latency > 450ms
- Create a second alert for error rate > 1%
- Set both to evaluate over a 5-minute window
- Configure notifications via email or Slack

5. **Configure automatic rollback**
- Create a Cloud Function or Workflow triggered by the alert
- The function updates the URL map to route 100% traffic back to v1

## Minimal IAM Roles
- **Cloud Build Service Account**: `roles/cloudbuild.builds.builder`
- **Cloud Run Admin**: `roles/run.admin`
- **Compute Load Balancer Admin**: `roles/compute.loadBalancerAdmin`
- **Monitoring AlertPolicy Editor**: `roles/monitoring.alertPolicyEditor`
- **Cloud Functions Invoker**: `roles/cloudfunctions.invoker` (for rollback function)

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
This question tests the ability to design end-to-end progressive delivery using only Google-native tools, with real-time metrics, cross-region concerns, and safe rollback. It emphasizes the integration of CI/CD, traffic management, and observability.

## Key Concepts
- Progressive canary deployment across revisions with time-based traffic ramping
- Cross-region latency and error rate monitoring using Cloud Monitoring
- SLO-based alerting with automated rollback triggers
- Minimal IAM for deployment and operations

## Implementation Steps

### 1. Publish v2 to Artifact Registry
Build and push the container image using Cloud Build or a local Docker build:

```bash
# Option A: Using Cloud Build
gcloud builds submit --tag us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2 .

# Option B: Local build and push
docker build -t us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2 .
gcloud auth configure-docker us-docker.pkg.dev
docker push us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2
```

### 2. Deploy v2 with Traffic Split
Deploy the new revision and configure progressive canary traffic splitting:

```bash
# Deploy v2 revision
SERVICE_NAME=chat-gateway
gcloud run deploy $SERVICE_NAME \
  --image us-docker.pkg.dev/PROJECT_ID/chat-gateway/v2 \
  --region us-central1

# Get the v2 revision name
V2_REVISION=$(gcloud run revisions list --service $SERVICE_NAME --region us-central1 --format='value(name)' | head -1)
V1_REVISION=$(gcloud run revisions list --service $SERVICE_NAME --region us-central1 --format='value(name)' | tail -1)

# Apply traffic split: 10% to v2 for 8 minutes
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V2_REVISION=10%,$V1_REVISION=90%

# After 8 minutes, update to 30% for 16 minutes
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V2_REVISION=30%,$V1_REVISION=70%

# After 24 minutes total, promote v2 to 100%
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V2_REVISION=100%
```

### 3. Cross-Region Health Checks and Monitoring
Configure Cloud Monitoring to track regional metrics:

**Create SLOs:**
- **p95 Latency SLO:** Target threshold 350ms over 5-minute sliding window
- **Error Rate SLO:** Target threshold 99.5% (max 0.5% errors) over 5-minute window

**Alert Policy Configuration:**
```bash
# Create alerting policy for p95 latency
cat > latency-alert.json << EOF
{
  "displayName": "Chat Gateway p95 Latency",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "displayName": "p95 latency > 350ms",
      "conditionThreshold": {
        "filter": "resource.type=\"cloud_run_revision\" AND metric.type=\"run.googleapis.com/container latency\"",
        "aggregation": {
          "alignmentPeriod": "60s",
          "perSeriesAligner": "ALIGN_PERCENTILE_95"
        },
        "comparison": "COMPARISON_GT",
        "thresholdValue": 0.35,
        "duration": "300s",
        "trigger": {
          "count": 1
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "combiner": "OR",
  "enabled": true
}
gcloud alpha monitoring policies create --policy-from-file=latency-alert.json
```

```bash
# Create alerting policy for error rate
cat > error-alert.json << EOF
{
  "displayName": "Chat Gateway Error Rate",
  "conditions": [
    {
      "displayName": "Error rate > 0.5%",
      "conditionThreshold": {
        "filter": "resource.type=\"cloud_run_revision\" AND metric.type=\"run.googleapis.com/container/request_count\"",
        "aggregation": {
          "alignmentPeriod": "60s",
          "perSeriesAligner": "ALIGN_RATE"
        },
        "comparison": "COMPARISON_GT",
        "thresholdValue": 0.005,
        "duration": "300s",
        "trigger": {
          "count": 1
        }
      }
    }
  ],
  "combiner": "OR",
  "enabled": true
}
gcloud alpha monitoring policies create --policy-from-file=error-alert.json
```

### 4. Automated Rollback
When alerts trigger, shift traffic back to v1:

```bash
# Immediate rollback to v1 (100% traffic)
gcloud run traffic update $SERVICE_NAME \
  --region us-central1 \
  --to-revisions $V1_REVISION=100%
```

### 5. Minimal IAM Roles
Assign the following roles to the deployment/service account:

| Role | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `roles/run.invoker` | Allows traffic invocation to Cloud Run service |
| `roles/artifactregistry.reader` | Pull container images from Artifact Registry |
| `roles/monitoring.alertPolicyUser` | Create and manage alerting policies |

### 6. Testing Failover
1. **Manual test:** Deploy a faulty v2 revision with artificial delay, verify alerts trigger within 5 minutes
2. **Traffic simulation:** Use `hey` or `vegeta` to generate load and validate latency/error SLOs
3. **Rollback test:** Trigger the alert and confirm traffic shifts to v1 automatically (via Cloud Functions or GitHub Actions triggered by Pub/Sub alerts)

## Summary
This implementation uses Cloud Run traffic splitting for gradual rollout, Cloud Monitoring SLOs with burn-rate alerts for cross-region observability, and gcloud commands for traffic management—all requiring only Google-native services with minimal IAM permissions.

## Why This Is Asked
Tests ability to coordinate secret rotation with zero-downtime deployments using Google-native tooling and to automate rollback via observability.

## Key Concepts
- Secret Manager secret versions and access control
- Cloud Run secret-env-vars with version pinning
- Canary deployments with traffic splitting
- Cloud Monitoring alerting for SLO-based rollback triggers
- IAM least privilege and CMEK encryption requirements
- Automated rollback workflows

## Code Example
```bash
# 1. Create new secret version
echo "new-secure-password" > ./new-password.txt
gcloud secrets versions add DB_PASSWORD \
  --data-file=./new-password.txt \
  --project=PROJECT_ID

# Get new version number
NEW_VERSION=$(gcloud secrets versions list DB_PASSWORD \
  --project=PROJECT_ID \
  --limit=1 \
  --format='value(name)' | grep -o '[0-9]*')

# 2. Deploy new revision with pinned secret
gcloud run deploy inventory-service-v2 \
  --image=gcr.io/PROJECT_ID/inventory-service:latest \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --secret-env-vars=DB_PASSWORD=projects/PROJECT_ID/secrets/DB_PASSWORD/versions/$NEW_VERSION \
  --no-traffic

# 3. Implement 5% canary for 20 minutes
gcloud run services update-traffic inventory-service \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --to-revisions inventory-service-v1=95,inventory-service-v2=5

# Monitor and auto-rollback script
sleep 1200  # 20 minutes
# Check metrics and rollback if needed
if [[ $(check_metrics) == "fail" ]]; then
  gcloud run services update-traffic inventory-service \
    --region=us-central1 \
    --to-revisions inventory-service-v1=100
  gcloud secrets versions disable $NEW_VERSION --project=PROJECT_ID
fi

# 4. Monitoring alert policies
gcloud monitoring policies create \
  --notification-channels=projects/PROJECT_ID/notificationChannels/EMAIL_CHANNEL \
  --condition-duration=300s \
  --condition-filter='metric.type="run.googleapis.com/container/request_latency" AND resource.label.service_name="inventory-service"' \
  --condition-threshold-value=1.2 \
  --condition-threshold-comparison=COMPARISON_GT \
  --condition-trigger-count=1 \
  --condition-aggregations-alignment-period=60s \
  --condition-aggregations-per-series-aligner=ALIGN_PERCENTILE_95

# 5. Rollback commands
gcloud run services update-traffic inventory-service \
  --region=us-central1 \
  --to-revisions inventory-service-v1=100

gcloud secrets versions enable PREV_VERSION --project=PROJECT_ID
gcloud secrets versions disable $NEW_VERSION --project=PROJECT_ID

# IAM permissions
gcloud projects add-iam-policy-binding PROJECT_ID \
  --member="serviceAccount:PROJECT_NUMBER-compute@developer.gserviceaccount.com" \
  --role="roles/secretmanager.secretVersionAdder"
```

This ensures zero-downtime secret rotation with automated rollback based on SLO violations.

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked

Assesses practical experience wiring Secret Manager, Cloud Run, and Monitoring with Google-native tools. Focuses on secure access patterns and observable failures.

## Key Concepts

- Secret Manager integration with Cloud Run environment variables
- IAM least-privilege for service accounts
- Cloud Run deployment flow and secret mapping
- Log-based metrics and alerting in Cloud Monitoring

## Code Example

```javascript
// Bash-like commands (illustrative)
// 1) create secret
gcloud secrets create db-password --replication-policy=automatic
// 2) add version (password supplied securely)
gcloud secrets versions add db-password --data-file=- << 'EOF'
$DB_PASSWORD
EOF
// 3) grant access to Cloud Run SA
gcloud run services add-iam-policy-binding health-check \
  --member=serviceAccount:health-check-sa@PROJECT.iam.gserviceaccount.com \
  --role=roles/secretmanager.secretAccessor
// 4) deploy with secret
gcloud run deploy health-check --image gcr.io/PROJECT/health-check:latest \
  --region us-central1 --set-secrets DB_PASSWORD=db-password:latest
// 5) monitoring: create log metric and alert (simplified)
gcloud logging metrics create secret_retrieval_errors \
  --log-filter='resource.type="cloud_run_revision" textPayload:"Secret retrieval failed"'
gcloud beta monitoring policies create --conditions '...'
```

## Follow-up Questions

- How would you rotate the secret with zero-downtime?
- How would you test the alerting in a sandbox?
